title: After I hired my first tutor, a parent complained about the quality of their child's sessions.
description:
Three weeks after I hired my first tutor, a parent complained about the quality of their child's sessions.

The embarrassing part wasn't the complaint. It was that I had no way to properly address it, because I'd never actually written down what "good" looked like in the first place. 

I'd onboarded my tutor over one phone call, shared my expectations verbally, and called it done. 😅

If you're dealing with inconsistent tutor quality right now, this is almost certainly why.

Here's what needs to be in place, in this order:

Write your standards down. Not in your head, not in a casual chat - a proper documented reference so every tutor knows exactly what's expected before they step into a session.

Check in after the first week. Small problems caught early are a quick conversation. Left for a month, they become habits that are much harder to correct (and much more awkward to bring up).

Create a parent feedback loop. A short check-in after the first few sessions tells you things your tutor won't. It also shows parents you're paying attention to their child's experience, not just filling a slot.

Get these three things in place and tutor quality stops being something you're constantly chasing. 🙌🏼

I felt so bad for saying 'no' that I ended up hiring my first tutor. Within 6 months, my team had grown to 5 tutors, and within a couple of years, I had 50+ tutors on my team!  
 
It's been a rollercoaster of a journey. I've been awarded Anthill 30under30, Victorian Younger Achievers Finalist, spoken at TEDx, and been blessed with so much more.  
 
Not going to lie, business is HARD. That's why I want to share my learnings and experiences with you, because I wish I had a tutor mentor who could accelerate my path to success, rather than struggling through all the mistakes I made during my journey. Lisa's Study Guides, my tuition and study guide business has made 1 million+ over the last 2 years, and I've just started my second business, Tutorboss, helping tutoring business owners build and scale their businesses.

title: Your next great hire might be closer than you think. 👀
description:
Your next great hire might be closer than you think. 👀

Many tutors I know go straight to Seek or Indeed when they’re hiring. 
When I first started hiring for Lisa’s Study Guides, I did that too. 
But honestly? It didn't work out great. 😅

Over time, and after helping 400+ tutors scale their teams, I've realised the most reliable, aligned tutors rarely come from job boards. They usually come from places much closer to you. 

If you’re currently looking to scale your team, here's where I'd actually start 👇
🙌🏼 University job boards: Recent grads just sat through the same exams, and they can relate to what your students are going through. 

🙌🏼 Word of mouth: This one’s my favourite, ask your best tutors if they know anyone! They’ll usually know other like-minded people who share the same work ethic and values. 

🙌🏼 Your past students: Look for your past students who smashed their exams! They already know your methodology, they've seen the results, and they believe in what you do. 

🙌🏼 LinkedIn and Facebook groups: An oldie but a goodie, this is especially helpful for finding tutors around your local area.

title: "I'm fine. I'm FINE!" 🫠

As your tutoring business grows, you have to learn to LEAD a business. Not just MANAGE a team of tutors.

title: I mean, respectfully... that's not quite how this works. 😅
description:
I mean, respectfully... that's not quite how this works. 😅

But you know what? In my early days, I would have said yes anyway. 🙈
Because when you're just starting out, every enquiry feels like a super big deal, and you'll do almost anything to close it. 

Discount your rates. Squeeze in extra sessions. 
Smile through the awkward "can we negotiate?" conversations and tell yourself, "it's fine, just this one time."

I remember sitting on calls, secretly hoping they wouldn't push back on the price. 
Laughing nervously when they did. 
Caving way too quickly because the thought of losing a potential student felt worse than undercharging.

But here's what I've learned: 
The awkwardness doesn't come from your pricing. It comes from attracting the wrong people in the first place.
When your marketing speaks to the right parents, the ones who already understand the value of what you offer, the price conversation almost takes care of itself.

Take one of the tutors I worked with, Sujin, for example. 
Once she built a system that consistently brought in quality leads, things started to shift. 
She was able to raise her rates. She could filter out parents who try to haggle or ghost mid-conversation. And she filled her calendar with students who genuinely valued her work and paid her what she was worth.

Her revenue more than doubled. And she was just so much happier. 🥹

If you're still saying yes to leads that make you feel uncomfortable just to close them, it might be time to build a system that brings in the RIGHT students. At the rate you actually deserve. 😉

title: If I were starting my tutoring business again in 2026,
description:
If I were starting my tutoring business again in 2026, I wouldn’t waste a single minute stressing about logos, colour palettes, or posting every day like my life depended on it.
 
I’d fix one thing first… knowing exactly what to do the moment someone says, “I’m interested.”
Because honestly? That used to send me spiralling.
 
I’d get a DM, an email, a casual “this sounds amazing!” and suddenly my brain would turn into a loading screen.
 
Do I send prices?
Do I book a call?
Do I repeat myself again?
Do I… pretend I didn’t see it?
 
And surprise surprise, the convo went nowhere.
Not because they weren’t interested, but because I had zero system and way too much panic.
 
This is why I keep saying: you don’t need more leads… you need clarity.
 
So if you’re sitting there thinking:
“I get interest but barely convert.”
or

You don’t need to be smoother, more confident, or more ‘salesy’.
